title.narrative: World Bank Umbrella Facility for Trade
World Bank Umbrella Facility for Trade

description.narrative:
Nytt stöd till Världsbanksgruppens nya övergripande handelsfond, "Umbrella Facility for Trade" (UF-Trade). UF-Trade avser ersätta tidigare multigivarfonder utifrån en heltäckande handelsstrategi och ett sammanhängande resultatramverk.
Världsbanksgruppen med sitt mandat och stora kapacitet har möjlighet att ta ett helhetsgrepp kring handelsrelaterat utvecklingssamarbete. Genom policypåverkan, analyser, implementering samt finansiering har de förutsättningar som ingen annan aktör har.
UF-Trade bygger fortsatt på Världsbanksgruppens handelsstrategi och dess tematiska områden. Dessa är: i) konkurrenskraft och diversifiering; ii) handelsprocedurer, logistik och handelsfinansiering; iii) stöd för marknadstillträde och internationellt handelssamarbete; samt iv) hantering av chocker och stärkt inkluderande fattigdomsminskning. Utöver dessa har globala värdekedjor, regional integration och tjänstehandel identifierats som högprioriterade områden. Dessa liksom ett ökat fokus på bland annat jämställdhetsfrågor utgör ett tematiskt fönster som fördelas enligt:
- Regionala och nationella insatser - "just-in-time" för hastigt uppkomna behov - globala frågor såsom forskning, påverkansarbete och framtagandet av olika verktyg
Världsbanksgruppen har presenterat ett förslag på arbetsområden och aktiviteter under sex år med en totalt önskad budget på 180 miljoner USD. Svenskt stöd till UF-Trade föreslås med 90 miljoner SEK för initialt tre år. För de tre första åren är finansiering på ungefär 45-50 miljoner USD utlovade av Sverige, Nederländerna, Storbritannien, Schweiz och Norge vilket innebär att UF-Trade idag är underfinansierat gentemot önskad budget. Finansieringen för de avslutande tre åren kan vara avhängigt ytterligare givare samt resultat under de första åren.
Medlen ska fördelas på olika "kuvert" eller finansieringsfönster enligt följande fördelning:
1. Regionalt och nationellt arbete som kommer innebära majoriteten av aktiviteter beräknas erhålla 65% av tillgängliga medel. 2. Globala frågor och insatser relaterat till forskning, påverkansarbete globalt samt metod- och verktygsutveckling får 30% av tillgängliga medel. 3. Det sista fönstret som benämns "just-in-time" ger utrymme för hastigt uppkomna behov och till det avsätts högst 5% av budgeten.
Givarna har också kommit överens med Banken att 60% av tillgängliga medel ska fokuseras på Afrika söder om Sahara och andra låginkomstländer.
Då den övergripande budgeten utgör en grund för projekt och programprioriteringar finns ingen detaljerad budget för hela fonden vilket är normalt för en trust fund på exempelvis Världsbanken. Däremot finns det kriterier och tematiska prioriteringar för vad medlen får användas till. Majoriteten av pengarna går till analytiskt arbete i form av studier och behovsanalyser, forskning, utveckling av verktyg och indikatorer. Det sker som nämnts på nationell, regional och global nivå där användandet kan vara normativt eller bidra till global dialog eller som underlag för vidare implementering av större gåvo eller låneprojekt. Världsbanksgruppens administrationskostnad baseras på en standard på 17%.
Inom UF-Trade kommer ett fönster finansiera aktiviteter under Världbanksgruppens "Trade Facilitation Support Program" (TFSP). TFSP:s funktion är att hjälpa utvecklingsländer med implementeringen av WTO:s Trade Facilitation Agreement. Det innebär att förenkla tull- och handelsprocedurer för att sänka transport- och transaktionskostnader i gränsöverskridande handel vilket utgör ett stort bekymmer för många utvecklingsländer. Utöver ovan nämnda givare bidrar även USA, Kanada och EU till TFSP som i dagsläget har en total budget på 36 MUSD. Sverige föreslår att 15 MSEK av det totala stödet till UF-Trade öronmärks till TFSP.
Mot bakgrund att den inte finns en detaljerad budget i detta skedde anser Sida ändå att budgeten framstår som rimlig och berättigad samt att det finns en systematik för hanteringen av budgetfrågor både på projektnivå och aggregerad nivå. Givarna har också möjlighet att påverka styrningen av budgeten i dialog med Världsbanksgruppen.
Sida och Världbanksgruppen avser använda avtalsmallen för multigivarfonder som förhandlades med Världsbanken inom CGOP, med justeringar för att innefatta International Finance Corporation IFC. Både Världsbanken och IFC skriver under avtalet.

Support to World Bank Umbrella Trust Fund for Trade. Will replace existing trust funds under the World Bank Trade Strategy and with one integrated results framework.
The World Bank Group, with its mandate and large capacity, has the opportunity to take a comprehensive approach to trade-related development cooperation. Through policy influence, analyses, implementation and financing, they have conditions that no other actor has.
UF-Trade continues to build on the World Bank Group's trade strategy and its thematic areas. These are: i) competitiveness and diversification; ii) trade procedures, logistics and trade finance; iii) support for market access and international trade cooperation; and iv) management of shocks and strengthened inclusive poverty reduction. In addition to these, global value chains, regional integration and trade in services have been identified as high priority areas. These, as well as an increased focus on, among other things, gender equality issues constitute a thematic window which is distributed according to:
- Regional and national efforts - "just-in-time" for rapidly arising needs - global issues such as research, advocacy work and the development of various tools

The intended effect of the development contribution is based on the World Bank Group's "twin goals" to increase shared prosperity, and the eradication of extreme poverty. According to the theory of change, more and better jobs, increased trade flows and raised productivity, contribute to increased incomes and to achieve these goals. The World Bank Group (WBG) analysis underpinning this theory of change, identifies a number of challenges that limit the possibilities of achieving these goals. Examples of challenges include weak diversification, high transaction and trading costs, limited market access, and the poor being those who are hardest hit by trade shocks and exclusion.
The objective of the Umbrella Facility for Trade (UFT) is to provide support to developing countries towards integrating them in the global economy while increasing trade. It is based upon and supports the implementation of the World Banks Groups trade strategy which focuses on four main pillars: i) trade competitiveness and diversification ii) trade facilitation and transport logistics iii) market access and international trade cooperation and, iv) managing shocks and promoting greater inclusion.
Through a number of different activities at both the country and the global level, the World Bank Group contributes to creating more competitive and open markets, export diversification, reduce trading costs, strengthened capacity in policy making and, not least, an increased and upgraded participation in global value chains. Activities supported by the UFT include analyses and research, technical assistance, development of methods and tools, and the establishment of partnerships and dialogues.
The specific goals of the Umbrella Facility for Trade are to: increase the number of WBG projects that incorporate trade expand the testing, experimentation, research, and sharing of new ideas on trade gather, document, and disseminate results, data, and knowledge on trade related issues and increase the WBGs voice on global trade issues through enhanced global partnerships and engagements.
Through the UFT support is also channeled to the WBGs Trade Facilitation Support Programme (TFSP) which form an integral part of the contribution. Its objective is to improve cross border trade environments and support the full and effective implementation of the World Trade Organizations Trade Facilitation Agreement (WTO TFA).

description.narrative:
Since inception 2017, 376 activities were launched in over 120 countries with support from the UFT 1.0, totaling US$ 80.9 million (including TFSP supported activities as well as DATA Fund activities channeled under the UFT 1.0). UFT 1.0 contributed in scaling up work on trade at the WBG as indicated by the evaluation in 2022 that found that it had successfully leveraged WB lending and trade work, also crowding in WBG staff resources over the regular budget.
1) Achievements related to the specific goals of UFT
The UFT specifically seeks to leverage WBGs trade work in order to increase the number of WBG projects that incorporate trade expand the testing, experimentation, research, and sharing of new ideas on trade gather, document, and disseminate results, data, and knowledge on trade related issues and increase the WBGs voice on global trade issues through enhanced global partnerships and engagements
Catalyzing World Bank lending to trade at country level:
UFT 1.0-supported activities directly informed US$25.6 billion of World Bank lending operations (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 13, Dox 15/001180- 284). For instance activities supported by TFSP informed prior actions on trade facilitation in several country specific loans, including Ukraine where the trade facilitation component supported amounted to USD 166 million. (World Bank, Trade Facilitation Support Program Annual Report FY 24, 2024, p. 31, DOX 15/001180-265).[M1]
Leveraging of World Bank-own resources to support trade:
Since the start of the program, 76 percent of UFT-supported activities on trade were complemented by the World Banks own financial resources, totaling US$56.4 million. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 13, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
Incorporating gender into trade:
The UFT 1.0 supported several flagship reports on trade and gender. For instance, the WBG in collaboration with WTO published Women and Trade: The Role of Trade in Promoting Womens Equality. The data collected was used by the Africa Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA) Secretariat and has informed WBG country support to the AfCFTA negotiations in identifying potential implications of the agreement on employment opportunities and wages of female workers. The UFT 1.0 also supported the inclusion of gender components within Country Economic Memorandums (CEMs) and Trade Competitiveness Diagnostics (TCDs) to help ensure trade more equally benefits women. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 13-14, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
Climate/environment and trade:
The UFT 1.0 supported the development of new toolkits to analyze the nexus between trade and climate. These diagnostics analyze the impact of climate change and mitigation policies on developing countries export competitiveness; the EUs carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM); anti-deforestation trade policies; the impact of water scarcity on agricultural trade; and the impact of climate change on tourism. For example, a CBAM Exposure Index was developed to help developing countries prepare and adjust to climate change regulations covering 120 countries. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 14-15, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
2) Achievements towards the four pillars of the WBG Trade Strategy
Pillar 1: Trade Competitiveness and Diversification
Pillar 1 aims to support domestic reforms for creating conducive policy environments for sustainable growth and creating more and better jobs by leveraging global trade opportunities. Under this pillar, the WBG helps governments to reap the gains from open trade, strengthen their market through diversification, and maximise their trade competitiveness by, for example, reviewing trade policies to remove biases about importing and exporting, and provide support to government interventions targeting specific market, policy, and institutional failures.
On an overall level, there was a consistent increase in policy adoption (recommended laws, regulations, amendments, or codes enacted), with a cumulative total of 236 since inception, indicating progress of the UFT 1.0 in influencing regulatory framework reform. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 55, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
Support to the African Continent Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA) is a good example under this pillar. The AfCFTA presents a significant opportunity for Africa to enhance regional trade integration, offering benefits such as expanded market access, investments, and free movement of people, which are expected to bolster growth, reduce extreme poverty, and alleviate hunger. By 2035, if the AfCFTA is fully implemented, the WBG estimates it could raise incomes by 9 percent and lift 50 million people out of extreme poverty.
With support from the UFT 1.0, the WBG helped the African Union Secretariat to build its own capacity to support implementation of the agreement. At the country level, the WBG provided support through capacity building and the design of effective monitoring of implementation of AfCFTA commitments to help countries leverage the opportunities the agreement could bring.
For instance, the WBG supported Rwanda in implementing the AfCFTA Trade in Services Protocol. The work identified non-conforming measures and discussions with the government took place on the reforms that would be needed to implement the AfCFTA Trade in Services Protocol in priority sectors. The work also identified proposed or ongoing reforms that showcase the Government of Rwandas progress in implementing the AfCFTA Trade in Services protocol, for example:
• In financial services, foreign banks can only enter through a subsidiary. However, a new banking law that was approved on July 13, 2023, and was subsequently submitted to parliament, lifted the subsidiary requirement and allows direct branching of foreign established banks.
• In communication services, Rwanda once imposed stringent local data storage rules, which were regarded as limiting the cross-border supply of digital services. A new law on personal data and privacy came into force from October 2023 that removed these restrictions.
The removal of these restrictions is expected to substantially increase the level of competition in commercial banking and telecommunication services, potentially increasing the range of services offered to Rwandan businesses and individuals as well as lowering their prices. This will likely boost competitiveness in other sectors of the economy by lowering the cost of access to and increasing the variety of financial and telecommunication services. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 25-27, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
From a Swedish Aid & Trade perspective, given Swedish business interests in FinTech and Telecom, this shows how synergies are created by strengthening institutions and trade related polices. Regulatory reforms in trade, enabled by evidenced based dialogue made possible by global public goods in terms of trade data, indexes and databases, have the potential to mobilise considerable amounts of private sector capital investment while creating business opportunities for Swedish companies.
Another example is from Indonesia where UFT helped the Ministry of Finance to analyse non-tariff measures (NTMs). As a result of the work, the government revoked over 20 regulations covering pre-shipment inspections, reducing them to just six regulations and reducing the share of affected products to under three percent. Additionally, the government, to simplify import approvals, more than halved the associated regulations. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 33-34, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
Pillar 2: Trade Facilitation and Transport Logistics
Pillar 2 has the objective to ensure the efficient operation of border management processes as well as to reduce the costs of trade related transport, finance and logistics, and increase their timeliness and reliability.
This is of high significance as the WTO TFA has been estimated to have led to an USD 231 billion increase in trade globally between 2017 and 2019 alone (a total trade increase of 1.17 percent globally). This increase in trade is important because higher trade exposure correlates with increased employment and labor income. Evidence shows that trade facilitation reforms disproportionately benefit manufacturing and import-dependent sectors, which tend to be more labor-intensive. Preferential customs treatment and improved border processes enable firms to grow, hire more workers, and pay higher wages. For example, in Tunisia, firms in import-dependent sectors saw larger impacts on employment and wage bills following trade facilitation reforms and trade reforms in Indonesia increased Foreign Direct Investment by 23 percent in liberalized sectors, potentially generating 3.2 million new jobs by 2026. (World Bank Group, Trade Facilitation Support Program Semi Annual Report Phase 2, 2025, s. vi, Dox: 24/000682-63)
Increasing alignment with WTO's Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA): An external evaluation of TFSP assessed the program favourable, while identifying some shortcomings and recommendations that has been taken on-board by WB. Overall it stated that "The results of the Trade Facilitation Support Program suggest that the interventions have led to meaningful outcomes and impacts at a national and regional level" with reference to alignment with individual TFA measures for seven countries that was analyzed as part of the evaluation, using updated data since their baselines were collected. On average, alignment scores for these countries improved from 43% at baseline to 64%. World Bank, Trade Facilitation Support Programme Stocktaking & Learning Review Final Report, International Economics Consulting Ltd, 2024, p. 4, DOX 15/001180-260,) [M1]. Overall TFA alignment increased from 40.8% to 53.5% in TFSP countries were baselines and updated assessment were done. (World Bank, Trade Facilitation Support Program - 10 years of Facilitating Trade, 2025, page 9, Dox 15/001180- 280).[M1].
Reducing time to comply with border processes - generating private sector saving in Sida partner countries: TFSP supported reforms have significantly reduced the time to comply with import and export clearance /control requirements by 21 percent across its portfolio. Furthermore, efficiency gains from time reduced in the cargo clearance process, combined with reductions in trade-related fees and charges, have resulted in an estimated USD 110 million in private sector savings. (World Bank, Trade Facilitation Support Program - 10 years of Facilitating Trade, 2025, page 4, Dox 15/001180- 280).[M1]
TFSP helped mobilize financing for a greater scope of trade facilitation reforms. TFSP-funded activities have been leveraged into 25 different lending instruments across 23 countries, totaling over 800 USD million. This support has strengthened the foundation for trade facilitation reforms, by enabling countries to have the resources needed to implement measures fully and effectively. (World Bank, Trade Facilitation Support Program - 10 years of Facilitating Trade, 2025, page 4, Dox 15/001180- 280).[M1]
A new Logistics Performance Index (LPI) driving evidenced based reform was developed with support from UFT 1.0. The old LPI launched in 2007 was based on surveys and hence essentially a perception index. This activity developed a new index that used objective measures of logistics performance by exploring several new and real time data sources from value chain and cargo operators. Access to novel supply chain data and data analysis techniques have been central to this work. This new dataset is helping policymakers develop informed policies and interventions in areas such as trade- and transport-related infrastructure, border management, and logistics services delivery. The LPI has been the entry point to reforms in many countries and several national connectivity strategies have used the LPI as a key performance indicator to track progress, for example in Indonesia, Vietnam, Morocco, Cambodia, Thailand, India, Uzbekistan, Türkiye, and Saudi Arabia. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 33-34, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
TFSP MENA-Window
REGMENA delegated 30 MSEK to GLOBEC from the regional strategy for development cooperation with Middle East and North Africa 2021-2025 to support a new component under UFT 1.0 called the Trade Facilitation Support Program in the MENA-region 2024-2026. Additional funding was agreed under an amendment to Sida's central agreement on UFT 2.0 to finance the remaining years as the UFT 1.0 ended 2024.
TFSP MENA was officially launched at the WTO Aid for Trade Global Review in June 2024 and the majority of the activities were implemented between July and December 2024. The launch brought together both the World Bank Global Director for Trade and the Sweden´s Ambassador to WTO together with representatives from both the private sector (ICC) and government representatives from Yemen and Egypt as well as trade facilitation experts. Activities started with Egypt, Jordan and Yemen and had a slow start in 2024, partly because the UFT were under transformation to the new UFT 2.0 which slowed down activities and partly due to challenges in the region.
In Egypt the activities continued to build on the already started UK-supported assistance to finalise an updated Time Release Study (TRS). The work included a review of import of sea cargo at major ports and one inland dry port. The TRS was finalized and discussed with the National Trade Facilitation Committee, NTFC and the Egyptian government.Workshop were held at NTFCs and the private sector to continue the dialogue under TFSP on TFA awareness, notification and measures needed to fulfil the agreement. Work on two critical documents was undertaken: Egypt National Trade Facilitation Strategy and Integrated Coordinated Risk Management Policy and Framework. (DOX 15/001180-272, Trade Facilitation Support Program in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, Progress Report July to December 2024, 2025, p. 13-14). [M1]
In Jordan work was undertaken to review the amendments to the Revised Customs Law (2024) to align with modern international standards, with particular focus on post-clearance audit (PCA) regime and legal basis to implement the receipt of pre-arrival of cargo information to facilitate for traders. This work will also facilitate risk-based approach for border clearance and thus reducing time and need for physical inspections by Jordan Customs Department (JCD), which leads to reduced trading time and costs. This is strongly correlated also to improved investment climate and overall integration into global value chains. This TA work was leveraged into a lending operation from the World Bank Trust Fund Jordan Growth and Competitiveness DPO which contributes to sustainability and is an advantage of the UFT. (DOX 15/001180-272, Trade Facilitation Support Program in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, Progress Report July to December 2024, 2025, p. 16).[M1]
In Yemen, the TFSP MENA supported participation in WTO`s Committee Meetings on Trade Facilitation in October 2024 that allowed the Yemen delegation to learn about latest developments and WTO TFA-implementation and LDC-assistance. Moreover, WTO TFA implementation plan and ratification process was supported, and work done on drafting a TFA Roadmap and Action Plan. (DOX 15/001180-272, Trade Facilitation Support Program in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, Progress Report July to December 2024, 2025, p. 7). [M1]
Pillar 3: Support for Market Access and International Trade Cooperation
The objective of this pillar was to reform trade policies that negatively impact developing countries, make international rules and institutions more supportive of the needs of developing countries, and evaluate what can be done to promote desirable integration and to protect the interests of those who are left out.
Aiding countries to navigate deep trade agreements (DTAs): DTAs encompass not only trade-related provisions but also address additional policy areas such as international investment and labor flows, as well as the protection of intellectual property rights and the environment. In capturing all the dimensions of DTAs and their connection to trade, the WBG helped equip developing countries with comprehensive tools to assess the implications of advanced provisions within trade agreements.
In total around 50 research papers and methodologies were produced under the activity in collaboration with academic experts and were presented during a webinar series on the economics of DTAs, at international conferences and seminars (such as the Global Trade Analysis Project (GTAP), African Union, London School of Economics, WTO Public Forum, Paris School of Economics). Data and analysis produced during the activity were used to support country work in Brazil, Dominican Republic, Georgia, Indonesia, Kenya, and Uzbekistan. For instance, two background studies were prepared on specific rules (e.g., public procurement, state owned enterprises) in trade agreements to support the Kenyan authorities in their ongoing negotiation of the trade agreements with the US. And a background paper was prepared on the effects of Georgias trade agreements on its export performance for the Georgia Country Economic Memorandum. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 37-39, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
Market access through compliance with EU regulation: Understanding and complying with the new EU deforestation regulation (EUDR) is another challenge for developing countries. In Peru exports of affected commodities including coffee, cocoa, wood, and palm oil account for 12 percent of its total exports to the EU. UFT 1.0-supported work guided the government to geolocate farmers that would be affected by the new regulation and craft a roadmap to ensure adherence to the EUDR, identifying key compliance gaps in Perus supply chains. UFT 1.0-supported work also led to a WBG lending operation that will help foster agricultural competitiveness and deforestation-free exports. As part of support provided, data collected and processed by the PPA (Padrón de Productores Agrarios y sus Organizaciones en las Cadenas de Valor) has also allowed the government to improve the provision and targeting of goods and services (e.g., seeds, fertilizers, extension services, training, credit) to all agricultural producers. The PPAs plot geolocation data and tree cover satellite imagery will verify that products come from non-deforested plots. This will allow for better monitoring of deforestation by government authorities and private stakeholders in value chains, enabling them to take early action to prevent further deforestation. As of June 2025, 2,100,000 producers had registered in the PPA, of which 45 percent are women. About 430,000 are producers of cocoa, palm oil, and coffee. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 29-30, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
Pillar 4: Managing Shocks and Promoting Greater Inclusion
Pillar 4 aims to address the reality of trade and to make distributional impacts of trade more visible, and the objective is to help policymakers understand the impacts and minimise adjustment costs and maximise benefits.
Using support from the UFT 1.0, the WBG helped countries to elaborate complementary policies that could improve the distributional effects of trade policy reforms through, for example: i) reducing distortions and strengthening the functioning of markets including factors of production; ii) reducing trade costs; and iii) speeding up labor market adjustment.
Leveraging trade for more and better jobs: With support from UFT, the WB published a Trade and Jobs flagship report, which inter alia was presented at the WTO Public Forum 2024. The reports main conclusions are that increased trade has been associated with more and better jobs over the last three decades. Not only has trade created more jobs but it has done so especially for women. It has also led to higher labor earnings on average as well as reduced wage inequality. And trade has been tied to more productive and salaried employment.
However, the analyses also provide support for some concerns. Unlike middle-income countries, trade in low-income countries does not seem to create large numbers of jobs or reduce wage inequality significantly. Moreover, the positive effects from trade have become weaker after the Global Financial Crisis. One key takeaway is that there is a need to strengthen the global rules-based system supporting trade.
While the report has a global focus, the new data and tools have already been applied to specific countries. Trade and jobs assessments have been undertaken so far in a Viet Nam 2045 GVC report; green industrial policy and GVCs reports for Bulgaria, Croatia, Poland, and Romania, and an India report on linking MSMEs to global markets. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 45-46, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
Informing and supporting the Ukraine Plan 2024-2027: a comprehensive monitoring effort to uncover the impact of the Russian invasion on the private sector in Ukraine was conducted. In particular, the activity deployed a variety of new tools to provide different perspectives on the impacts on firms within the context of the ongoing conflict. These tools included an in-country Business Pulse Survey of over 2,700 firms, a multinational corporation survey, and an innovative analysis of real time data on economic activity across multiple locations relying on satellite imagery data. Analytical work informed the WBs advice to the Government of Ukraine in the design of the Ukraine Plan 2024-2027, and in setting the business environment reform priorities of the Ukraine Reform Matrix 2024-2027. The Ukraine Plan 2024-2027 is co-financed by a dedicated EU support mechanism providing up to €50 billion for Ukraines recovery, reconstruction, and modernization efforts between 2024 and 2027.
Furthermore, the findings of both the first and second waves of private sector monitoring informed the design of the WB/IFC Resilient, Inclusive and Sustainable Enterprise RISE Program for Results (PforR) lending operation with cumulative disbursements totaling USD 250 million by the end of December 2024. Data from the WB report "Women-led Firms Through the War: Evidence from Ukraine" were also presented and highlighted to what extent PSD monitoring substantively contributed to advance the gender agenda in Ukraine by providing solid analytical evidence that women-led firms were hit harder by the war compared to men-led businesses. (World Bank, Trust Fund Completion Report - Umbrella Facility for Trade, 2026, page 46-48, Dox 15/001180- 284).[M1]
Examining Gender Dimensions to Trade Facilitation: To better understand how trade facilitation reforms impact traders at the firm level, particularly when disaggregated by the gender of the person leading the firm, the WBG through TFSP designed the Trade and Gender Survey. This initiative helps fill the data gaps on the nexus between trade facilitation and gender and provides insights to inform future project design and implementation with a view towards inclusivity. Across the surveys that have been completed, almost 9,500 importing / exporting firms and customs clearing agents were interviewed about their experiences in utilizing trade facilitation measures. (World Bank, Trade Facilitation Support Program - 10 years of Facilitating Trade, 2025, page 14, Dox 15/001180- 280).[M1]
OVERALL ASSESSMENT
UFT was initiated to catalyse the implementation of the WBGs Trade Strategy with the aim to increase the number of WBGs projects that incorporate trade and to increase the WBGs voice on global trade issues through enhanced global partnerships and engagement. The latest evaluation of UFT from 2022 acknowledge that UFT has delivered on its aim above, and noted the high relevance of the UFT and the improvements in management made compared to previous Trust Funds. Moreover, the recent external evaluation of the Trade Facilitation Support Program also highlights important achievement and overall finds that "The results of the Trade Facilitation Support Program suggest that the interventions have led to meaningful outcomes and impacts at a national and regional level."
It is thus assessed, as the results examples above also indicates, that UFT has contributed to the overall aim of enhancing developing countries participation in the global trading system, and thus, fostering inclusive and sustainable economic development and poverty reduction. The UFT has delivered significant results both in terms of leveraging WBG's work on trade and in terms of informing operations that address steps in the Theory of Change outlined for the program and framed by the WBG Trade Strategy. In comparison to previous support to trade at WB through the MDTF-TD2 there was significant progress in addressing trade from an inclusivity angle including a gender and environment/climate perspective with several important flagship studies and tools developed.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
